summary.headline: Sell a narrow SME workflow automation pilot; do not start with a speculative SaaS build.
summary.why_now: The 2025 UK business estimate counts 5.7m private-sector firms, mostly small; current cyber research also documents persistent small-business security gaps. These support a large prospect pool, not guaranteed demand.

top_opportunities.name: SME workflow automation retainers
top_opportunities.description: Implement and maintain one narrow workflow (lead intake, quoting, reminders, invoice chasing) using existing SaaS and modest AI.
top_opportunities.why_now: The UK had 5.7m private-sector businesses at start-2025, 99.18% small; this is a broad reachable buyer pool, not proof of willingness to pay.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local service SMEs with repetitive admin
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£900 initial tooling and setup; validate before spend
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks via direct outreach and paid pilot
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly maintenance/support retainer, typically £100–£400 per client (test pricing)
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong: software engineer can integrate tools quickly; selling and process discovery are the main work.
risks: Crowded generic AI pitch; differentiate by one measurable workflow.
Client data handling, API reliability and change requests can erode margin.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best overall: sell a fixed-scope paid workflow pilot before building software.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry capture for trades
top_opportunities.description: Mobile-first enquiry form, instant acknowledgement, routing and follow-up for trades firms losing leads while on jobs.
top_opportunities.why_now: Large base of small firms creates a practical niche, but no current source quantified missed-call losses; validate locally.
top_opportunities.buyer: Plumbers, electricians, roofers and small maintenance firms
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly hosting, monitoring and iteration; £50–£200 per site
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong: small web product plus integrations suits solo delivery.
risks: Lead volume and ROI vary by trade and geography.
top_opportunities.verdict: Sell lead response improvements, not a generic website.

top_opportunities.name: Cyber hygiene setup and monthly checks
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope baseline: MFA, backups, updates, access review and simple incident checklist; refer regulated certification work to qualified specialists.
top_opportunities.why_now: UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 reports attacks in 41% of micro and 50% of small firms; it also found basic controls remain uneven.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly check-in and maintenance; £75–£250 per month
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit, but requires careful boundaries and trust.
risks: Do not promise security or certification beyond competence.
Liability, sensitive access and customer trust create sales friction.
top_opportunities.verdict: Practical service demand signal, but sell only within demonstrable competence.

top_opportunities.name: Local-business website care and conversion service
top_opportunities.description: Refresh or maintain simple sites, booking/contact flows, analytics and local search basics on a fixed monthly plan.
top_opportunities.why_now: The 2025 business population estimate shows 5.64m small businesses; scale alone does not establish local digital-service demand.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local clinics, trades, hospitality and independent services
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Care plans and ongoing conversion changes; £50–£250 monthly
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong build fit; requires disciplined outbound and portfolio proof.
risks: Clients may churn if outcomes are not reported.
top_opportunities.verdict: Fast service revenue; package recurring care and measurable monthly reporting.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical micro-SaaS for compliance/admin
top_opportunities.description: Prototype one repeated job (document expiry reminders, inspection logs or client onboarding) for a tightly defined UK niche.
top_opportunities.why_now: Large small-business population supports niche exploration, but no evidence establishes demand for a specific product; interview first.
top_opportunities.buyer: One niche trade or small regulated service sector
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong engineering fit, but slower sales and product-market risk.
risks: Building before securing paid design partners.
Incumbents, compliance changes and support burden.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not build until at least three buyers commit to a paid pilot.

best_pick.name: SME workflow automation retainers
best_pick.why_it_wins: A tightly scoped service can be sold and delivered before substantial product investment, with a natural monthly support retainer.
validation_plan: Interview 10 firms in one niche about a single repetitive admin bottleneck; ask for a recent example and current workaround.
Offer a fixed-price paid pilot to at least three qualified prospects; proceed only if one pays and the workflow can be measured.
best_pick.first_offer: £300–£600 fixed-price setup of one workflow, followed by an optional £125–£250/month monitoring and improvement plan.
best_pick.mvp: One documented workflow using client-approved existing tools, one exception path, a short handover and baseline/outcome measurement; no custom platform.
customer_types: Small professional or appointment-based service firms
best_pick.do_today: Choose one niche; contact 15 local businesses with a specific workflow question and offer a paid pilot, avoiding claims of guaranteed savings.
